candidates.title: Forked PRT player computes claims in whatever cartesi-jsonrpc-machine PATH or CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE names, but every version check measures the in-process library (JSON-RPC client checks only the protocol version 0.9)
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (forked mode: prt.lua new_machine/new_forked_player/fork_server) and the machine API JSON-RPC client (jsonrpc_machine::check_server_version, spawn_server)
candidates.role: Support (PRT player, AUDIT.md table); the JSON-RPC client is machine API = honest operator only where a production node plausibly relies on it for a version check
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:997-1003 (new_machine: spawn_server + load + root-hash check only), prt.lua:3185-3192 (new_forked_player, all claims computed in spawned/forked servers), prt.lua:956-969 (assert_rolling_template compares against the client constant cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH, and is called only from the stored player's store_first_epoch_checkpoint, prt.lua:2758), doc/recipes/crisium.lua:128-132 (deployment check against the client constant); src/jsonrpc-machine.cpp:425-433 (check_server_version compares only JSONRPC_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR), src/jsonrpc-machine.cpp:480-483 (server binary from getenv CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE or PATH), src/jsonrpc-remote-machine.cpp:855-865 (get_version returns only the JSON-RPC protocol version, src/jsonrpc-version.hpp 0.9.0)
candidates.description: Two honest operators that run the same recipes can compute their claims with two different emulator builds without any check noticing. In forked mode the player never computes in-process: new_machine spawns 'cartesi-jsonrpc-machine' found through CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE or PATH, and every later machine is a fork of that server. The JSON-RPC client accepts any server whose JSON-RPC protocol version is 0.9 (check_server_version ignores the emulator version, marchid and uarch pristine hash); the protocol version is independent of the state transition function, so it does not change when the interpreter, uarch or verifier changes. The forked player itself performs no version check at all (only initial root hash equality), and the version checks that do exist in the recipes (crisium.lua's on-chain UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH comparison, assert_rolling_template) compare against cartesi.UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH of the Lua module loaded in the client process, never against machine:get_uarch_pristine_hash() of the server that executes. The only server-side guard is the load-time marchid comparison, which R1-R13-3 shows cannot distinguish builds of one release cycle (marchid 23 for all v0.23 pre-releases). So a server of a different build of the same cycle (for example the v0.23.0-test1 emulator next to a -test2 Lua module) computes mcycle and uarch claims under another transition function while the client-side referee model / verifiers and checks use the in-process build. The divergence is silent for mcycle claims (native interpretation) and surfaces only at the leaf, when the server's uarch differs from the template's pristine uarch (collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes 'not pristine') or when the in-process verifier rejects the server's log, i.e. after the honest claim is committed.
candidates.trigger: The operator's environment: a cartesi-jsonrpc-machine binary on PATH (or CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE) from another build than the Lua cartesi module, e.g. after a partial upgrade or a distro package next to a locally built module. No adversary action is needed; any adversary can then win the dispute against the diverged claim.
candidates.reachability: Always reachable in forked mode (prt.lua 'honest' role without an epoch directory, vg.lua-style demos); crisium's production-like path uses the stored player, which computes in-process and is checked against the same library, so it is NOT affected. A production node that uses remote JSON-RPC machines and relies on the client's connect-time check would be affected the same way; the API does allow a correct check (machine.get_uarch_pristine_hash and read_reg('marchid') go to the server), so the client is not unable to detect, it only does not.
rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? Section 4 trusts 'the emulator binary and its build'; but R13 requires 'The honest operator must be able to detect and refuse a mismatch between its build and a deployment. The check must refuse every pairing of its build with a deployment of another released version.' The trigger is a host configuration the recipes do not detect, not an untrusted party calling the API, so it is not excluded by the API exclusions. If triage reads a mismatched PATH as 'not running the emulator correctly', it is out of scope.

2 Role: the forked PRT player is Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support'). It stands in for the honest operator. The JSON-RPC client check is machine API: honest operator only if a production node plausibly relies on check_server_version as its version check; when unsure give both.

3 High/Medium cases: High lists 'A node that cannot detect a version mismatch, while every node in fact runs the deployment's version.' The forked player cannot detect a mismatch between the server it computes with and the build it checks/verifies with. Shown only by a support component, section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for' -> Medium. If the mismatch actually occurs, the honest claim is wrong (completeness failure, R1/R13), which would be Critical in the honest-operator role, still capped at Medium for support.

4 Critical: only if a production node computes claims through spawn_server/connect_server and relies on the JSON-RPC client's version check (R13 obligation violated on the honest operator's path). The validator nodes are out of scope, so this reading is unlikely.

5 Low: if triage holds that the machine API already lets callers check the server (get_uarch_pristine_hash is remote) and the forked player is a demonstration, the residual is a Low diagnostics/portability gap.
candidates.claimed_severity: Medium (support player standing in for the honest operator); Low if only the demo uses forked mode; High/Critical only if a production node relies on check_server_version
candidates.threat_to_goal: Goal of section 1 assumes the honest operator computes the claim the state transition function defines. Here the transition function actually used for the claim is selected by an environment variable/PATH outside every check, so two honest operators (forked vs stored, or two forked hosts) commit to different claims for the same template and inputs, and the one whose server differs from the deployment loses at the leaf (completeness failure).
candidates.evidence: Code reading of the cited lines. Experiments (e1.lua, e2.lua in the scratch dir) confirm that local and spawned/forked JSON-RPC machines of the SAME build agree exactly (collect_mcycle_root_hashes period 2^20 and 2^10, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, root hashes, also after fork_server), so the only divergence source on this path is the build the server comes from. get_version on the server returns {major=0,minor=9,patch=0} irrespective of EMULATOR_VERSION/MARCHID. No second emulator build was available to show an actual divergence (rebuilding was not allowed).
candidates.test_idea: Point CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE at a stub (Python, I/O on the fd passed as argv[1]) that answers get_version with 0.9.0, machine.load, machine.get_root_hash with the template hash and machine.get_uarch_pristine_hash with a different hash (as a server of another build would). Assert that prt.new_machine/new_forked_player (and cartesi_jsonrpc.spawn_server or connect_server in a version-checking mode) refuses the server; today it accepts. Equivalently assert that the player compares machine:get_uarch_pristine_hash() of its server with the deployment's UARCH_PRISTINE_STATE_HASH and the server's emulator version/marchid with its own.

not_covered: SIMD dispatch on non-x86 hosts (aarch64 NEON, RISC-V V, wasm) and the run-time ifunc selection itself: tested only by compiling the x86 generic/AVX2/AVX-512 variants of keccak_256_context<1,2,4,8> and sha_256 (1..16 lanes) as separate builds against the 1-lane byte path, 2000 random words and word pairs each: all identical (kt.cpp).

Thread counts: compared concurrency 1/4/default and phtc_size 1/2/4096 (with 4 threads at phtc 1) on collect_mcycle_root_hashes and collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes of the valid template: all identical; no ThreadSanitizer run of the OpenMP regions in hash_tree::return_updated_dirty_pages/update_and_clear_dense_node_entries.
Host page sizes other than 4 KiB (16/64 KiB): only reasoned (os::mapped_memory partial-page memset, read-only refusal already R1-R1-2); no run on such a host.
Big-endian hosts: the interpreter and hashers static_assert little-endian, so they do not build; not explored further.

Compiler/standard-library variation (clang/libc++, gcc versions, -march=native builds, LTO): not built; only scanned for UB-sensitive builtins (clz guarded in soft-float, ilog2 only on non-zero masks) and std::sort/unordered containers (ordering does not reach hashes).

Locale and environment: no setlocale anywhere in src or recipes; only CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE, CARTESI_JSONRPC_MACHINE_LOG_LEVEL, OMP_* and recipe PRT_* variables are read; locale-dependent Lua string comparison not exercised.
Stored vs forked PRT player claim equality on misbehaving guests and across reopen_epoch_directory/revert_interrupted_input/agreed-pair restarts: read, not run (still uncovered from earlier rounds).

Interrupt-check invariant (native inner loop vs uarch's per-mcycle raise_interrupt_if_any) was checked for CSR writes, CLINT, PLIC and privilege changes by reading only; no randomized differential run.

Store/load history: one test of collect_mcycle_root_hashes in two parts across store (sharing none) and store+SHARING_ALL load/run/destroy/sync/reload with the partial bundle carried, equal to the whole run; no test with replace_memory_range, clone_stored or the hash-tree files of a reloaded directory beyond that.
JSON-RPC: local vs remote vs fork_server equality tested on one input; rebind/swap, remote store/load and large results were not tested; no mixed-build pair was available.
Dave contracts, referee model and guest tools: not examined under this angle (they do not compute claims).
